name: Waris
confidence_why: The only description of Waris stress, the SIL Organised Phonology Data sheet (2004, data checked by the Waris fieldworker Robert Brown), states that stress is phonemic and gives minimal pairs such as 'aval 'ant sp.' against a'val 'mother' and 'sagal 'singsing' against sa'gal 'rat sp.', and nothing contradicts it: Brown's 1988 article and 1990 grammar sketch say nothing about stress, and Seiler's 1985 report of no contrastive stress concerns the sister language Imonda, not Waris.

catalog_quote: Suprasegmentals (tone, stress, length) Stress is phonemic. 'aval 'ant sp.' 'sagal 'singsing' a'val 'mother' sa'gal 'rat sp.' [...] Conventions: Phonological [...] /æ/ occurs only in stressed syllables with bilabials and is rare; some phonetical [æ] are the result of /ɑ/ raised by nearby /u/. [...] Conventions: Orthographic Phonetic prenasalization is written medially and finally. Stress is not written. [...] Phonetic schwa [ə] occurring in unstressed syllables is written as < a > or < e > according to insight gained from affixed forms as to what the underlying vowel is: sa [sə] 'coconut' but samba [saᵐbə] 'coconut + focus'. Where it is not clear whether the underlying form is /ɑ/ or /e/, it is arbitrarily taken to be /ɑ/.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Word stress is lexically contrastive (phonemic): disyllables can be stressed on either syllable, as shown by minimal pairs 'aval 'ant sp.' vs a'val 'mother' and 'sagal 'singsing' vs sa'gal 'rat sp.'; no default position is stated. Unstressed vowels may reduce to schwa; /ae/ is confined to stressed syllables. Stress is not marked in the orthography.
new_statements.exceptions: None; only the two minimal pairs are given, with no statement of a default or majority pattern.
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level citation forms (isolated lexical items in an OPD sheet); no tone or contrastive length reported; the 1990 grammar sketch separately says intonation is clause-level with low functional load.
new_statements.identity_note: The OPD describes Waris under the self-designation Walsa, data from Wasengla area, Sandaun Province, PNG side (major villages Dauatindi, Ivmi, Wainda, Kwek, Namolla); Brown 1990 notes four major dialects plus speakers in Kecamatan Waris, Indonesian Papua. Same language as Glottolog wari1266 / ISO wrs; no sub-dialect glottocode applies.

readall_conflicts: No direct conflict for Waris: the single listed work (Seiler 1985) says nothing about Waris stress; its statement that stress and tone are non-contrastive with roughly equal stress on all syllables is made for Imonda only (p. 10, sec. 2.2). The existing Waris statement (SIL PNG Organised Phonology Data 2004, p. 4: 'Stress is phonemic', minimal pairs 'aval 'ant sp.' / a'val 'mother', 'sagal 'singsing' / sa'gal 'rat sp.'; 'Stress is not written', p. 5) therefore stands unchallenged. There is a family-level tension worth flagging: the closest documented relative (Imonda, once classed as a Waris dialect) is reported as having no contrastive stress, whereas Waris is reported as having phonemic stress; both may be right, and Seiler's sound-system chapter is admittedly brief ('only the main points', sec. 2.1), so this is not a contradiction of the catalog.
